children: FreeCast, Inc. (

) ("FreeCast" or the "Company"), a media technology company providing a cloud-based Platform-as-a-Service ("PaaS") for streaming entertainment, advertising and digital media monetization, today announced financial results for its fiscal first quarter ended September 30, 2026.
The Company reported year-over-year revenue growth of 29%, advertising revenue growth of 42.5%, and a quarter-end cash balance of approximately $19.1 million following its July 2026 financing.

The results reflect FreeCast's continued development of its advertising business as management focuses on advancing enterprise distribution relationships into commercial deployments and expanding opportunities for recurring platform monetization.
Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Financial Highlights
Total revenue increased 29% year over year
Advertising revenue increased 42.5% year over year
Gross margin was 73.0%
Registered users increased 24% year over year to approximately 1.23 million.
Cash totaled $19.1 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $8.9 million at June 30, 2026.
Net loss was approximately $3.3 million, or $(0.07) per share
CEO Commentary: Advancing Toward Commercial Monetization

"Fiscal 2027 represents an important stage in FreeCast's evolution as we focus on converting years of technology development, infrastructure investment and enterprise relationships into commercial deployments and recurring monetization opportunities," said William Mobley, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of FreeCast.

"During our first quarter, total revenue increased 29% and advertising revenue grew 42.5% year over year. Following our July financing, we ended September with approximately $19.1 million in cash, providing financial resources to support the next phase of our commercialization strategy.

"FreeCast was designed around a fundamental opportunity in the global media industry. Telecommunications providers, broadband operators, property owners and major consumer brands already maintain direct relationships with substantial customer audiences, yet many lack a comprehensive platform for delivering and monetizing streaming entertainment.

"Our technology enables these organizations to introduce their own branded media experiences across connected devices, combining free television, premium subscriptions, advertising, content discovery and digital commerce within one software platform.
"Rather than competing to acquire consumers one subscriber at a time, our strategy is to work with enterprises that already serve established customer bases.
"We believe this approach offers an opportunity to expand distribution while creating multiple potential revenue sources from participating customers.

"Our priorities are clear: advance signed agreements into live deployments, increase activated users, expand advertiser participation and manage operating expenses as we work toward building a larger recurring revenue base.

"We believe FreeCast has established a technology foundation and commercial relationships that position us to pursue these opportunities. Our focus is now on disciplined execution and measurable results."
Commercialization Strategy: Connecting Distribution, Consumers and Revenue

FreeCast operates a software-based media and monetization platform designed to enable enterprises to offer branded streaming entertainment and related services without developing and maintaining a comprehensive streaming technology infrastructure themselves.
The Company's platform integrates content discovery, free ad-supported television, premium subscription management, advertising technology, digital payments and commerce capabilities.
FreeCast's business model is designed to create multiple potential revenue opportunities through a common technology platform, including:
Advertising: Local, regional and national advertising monetization through the Company's Zer0Gap advertising platform.
Premium subscriptions: Subscription distribution, management and related transaction opportunities through FreeCast's integrated marketplace.
Entertainment transactions: Potential revenue from pay-per-view programming, premium content, sports and other digital entertainment offerings.
Enterprise services: Branded media experiences, communications and additional services offered through distribution partners.
Digital commerce: Potential transaction and commerce opportunities integrated into the consumer viewing experience.
FreeCast's commercialization strategy follows a progression from signed enterprise agreements to technical integration, commercial deployment, consumer activation and revenue generation.

Management believes that adding revenue-producing deployments over time may support a growing base of recurring business activity, although the timing and financial contribution of individual agreements will vary.
Three Primary Enterprise Markets
FreeCast is concentrating its enterprise distribution strategy across three principal commercial markets.
1. Telecommunications, Mobile and Broadband Providers
Estimated commercial development cycle: 6–18 months

FreeCast enables mobile network operators, mobile virtual network operators, telecommunications companies, satellite connectivity providers, fiber networks and internet service providers to introduce branded entertainment and media services to their existing customers.
These organizations control essential consumer connectivity infrastructure and maintain established customer relationships.
FreeCast's platform is designed to provide additional opportunities for customer engagement, advertising monetization, premium subscriptions and digital transactions.
2. Multi-Dwelling Properties and Managed Communities
Estimated commercial development cycle: 6–24 months
FreeCast provides media and entertainment technology for apartments, condominiums, residential communities, hospitality properties, healthcare facilities, campuses and community developers.
The platform enables property operators and service providers to offer integrated television, streaming entertainment and community services to residents and guests.
Commercial deployment timing depends on property readiness, integration requirements, contractual arrangements and, for new developments, construction and occupancy schedules.
3. Major Consumer Brands and Organizations
Estimated commercial development cycle: 12–24 months
FreeCast enables membership organizations, shopping clubs, municipalities, media brands and other enterprises with established audiences to offer branded streaming and digital media platforms.
These relationships are designed to support customer engagement and potential advertising, subscription, transaction and commerce revenue opportunities.

The development cycles above represent management estimates and are not guaranteed implementation or revenue commencement dates. Actual timing will depend on contractual, technical, operational and market factors.
First Quarter Operational Highlights
During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, FreeCast advanced several initiatives supporting its platform distribution and monetization strategy:

FreeCast Cities: Announced its strategy to establish locally focused streaming experiences across the 210 U.S. designated market areas, supporting local entertainment discovery and geographic advertising opportunities.
Zer0Gap Advertising: Expanded the capabilities of its advertising platform, including AI-driven audience targeting designed to support more relevant advertising opportunities.
Brazilian Programming: Entered into an agreement with RBTI to bring 28 Brazilian television channels to the FreeCast platform, supporting international content expansion.
Investor News Channel: Assumed full control of Investor News Channel, supporting plans to relaunch and expand the channel's FAST distribution and programming.
Sports Content: Introduced an NFL-focused information destination as part of the Company's broader sports entertainment strategy.
These initiatives are intended to strengthen FreeCast's media offerings, advertiser capabilities and opportunities for consumer engagement as enterprise distribution expands.
Developments Subsequent to September 30, 2026
Following the close of the fiscal first quarter, FreeCast announced additional developments supporting its commercialization strategy.
Enterprise Distribution Expansion
FreeCast added Cajun Broadband, a Louisiana-based fiber and fixed wireless broadband provider, as a distribution partner, expanding its potential enterprise distribution opportunities.
Advertising Sales Development

The Company appointed Larry Watzman, a veteran broadcast advertising executive with experience involving FOX, Scripps and TEGNA-affiliated television operations, as Streaming Advertising Manager for Zer0Gap.
The appointment supports FreeCast's strategy to expand advertiser relationships, particularly among local and regional businesses seeking targeted streaming television advertising opportunities.
True Voice AI: Conversational Entertainment Discovery

FreeCast introduced True Voice AI, a conversational voice and chat discovery capability designed to help consumers search for movies, television series, sports and other entertainment across supported services.
The technology is currently being tested through FreeCast's web interface, with planned expansion to the FreeCast Watch App.
Management believes simplified entertainment discovery can support consumer engagement and improve the overall experience across FreeCast-powered platforms.
PayMeAds: Connecting Advertising Engagement to Consumer Value
FreeCast announced PayMeAds, a consumer engagement initiative targeted for launch December 1, 2026.
The program is designed to enable qualifying viewers to earn credits toward supported streaming subscription payments by watching eligible advertisements on free channels.
The initiative is intended to connect advertiser participation, consumer engagement and subscription activity within FreeCast's platform.
FreeCast Sports
The Company launched FreeCast Sports, expanding its sports-focused entertainment discovery and content offerings.
Industry Recognition
FreeCast received recognition from Media & Entertainment Business Review in connection with its streaming technology platform.
Commercial Progress and Operating Metrics
FreeCast believes that enterprise agreements, commercial deployments and consumer activation are important indicators of its progress toward generating revenue through its platform.

As disclosed in the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, the Company had 25 distribution partners representing a potential customer universe of approximately 31.2 million users, and a pipeline of 14 potential partners representing approximately 14.7 million potential customers.
Distribution partners represent enterprises with signed agreements to offer FreeCast's platform, including partners that may not yet have completed commercial deployment.

Partner-Enabled Addressable Customers (PEAC), the Company's measure of potential partner customer reach, represents the estimated audiences served by distribution partners and does not represent registered users, active subscribers, contracted revenue or guaranteed future revenue. Partner audiences may overlap.
Pipeline opportunities represent prospective commercial relationships that have not yet resulted in definitive agreements.
The Company intends to emphasize measurable commercial progress as its enterprise deployments and monetization activities develop.
Fiscal 2027 Business Priorities
FreeCast's principal operating priorities for the remainder of fiscal 2027 include:
Accelerating Commercial Deployments

Advancing existing enterprise relationships, including telecommunications, broadband, DIRECTV-related distribution and Starlink Business opportunities, through integration, implementation and commercial activation.
Expanding Advertising Revenue
Increasing advertiser participation through Zer0Gap, with particular emphasis on local and regional advertisers and opportunities associated with enterprise distribution partners.
Increasing Consumer Engagement
Continuing the development and deployment of consumer-facing capabilities, including True Voice AI, PayMeAds, FreeCast Cities, sports programming and unified entertainment discovery.
Expanding Revenue-Producing Enterprise Relationships
Working to convert signed agreements and prospective opportunities into live deployments, activated customers and monetization activity.
Maintaining Financial Discipline
Managing operating expenses and capital deployment while supporting commercial expansion and ongoing platform development.

Management believes the Company's existing technology infrastructure is designed to support additional enterprise deployments without requiring the construction of a separate comprehensive platform for each partner. Actual operating costs and margins will depend on deployment requirements, usage, contractual terms and other factors.
Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Financial Results
Revenue
Revenue increased 29% year over year to $252,312 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Advertising revenue increased 42.5% to $169,627, primarily reflecting advertising contracts secured during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, including the Company's Del Air agreement.
FAST revenue from related-parties increased 30.9% to $71,579.
Subscription revenue was $11,106, reflecting the Company's ongoing transition toward free consumer registration supported by advertising and additional monetization opportunities.
Gross Margin and Operating Expenses
Gross margin was 73.0%, compared with 73.4% in the prior-year period.

Operating expenses totaled approximately $3.45 million, compared with $2.95 million in the prior-year period, primarily reflecting increased sales and marketing activities and costs associated with operating as a public company.
Net Loss
The Company reported a net loss of approximately $3.3 million, or $(0.07) per share, compared with a net loss of approximately $2.9 million, or $(0.07) per share, in the prior-year period.
Liquidity and Capital Resources
FreeCast ended the quarter with approximately $19.1 million in cash, compared with $8.9 million at June 30, 2026.
During July 2026, the Company completed a private placement generating approximately $23.7 million in gross proceeds.
Net cash used in operating activities during the quarter was approximately $4.0 million, including approximately $0.5 million associated with reductions in accounts payable and accrued expenses.

Based on its current operating plan and available liquidity, management believes the Company has sufficient cash resources to fund planned operations for at least the next twelve months. This assessment remains subject to the assumptions, risks and uncertainties described in the Company's SEC filings.
About FreeCast
FreeCast, Inc. (

) is a media technology company providing a cloud-based Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) that enables telecommunications providers, mobile operators, broadband companies, property operators and major consumer brands to offer branded streaming entertainment and digital media services.

FreeCast's platform integrates live television, free ad-supported programming, premium streaming subscriptions, unified content discovery, advertising monetization, subscription management and digital commerce capabilities across connected devices.

The Company's enterprise distribution model is designed to help organizations with established customer relationships introduce media and entertainment services while creating potential new sources of advertising, subscription and transaction revenue.
For more information, visit www.freecast.com.
